utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Good morning to all. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. This is IT-01-47-A, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, I would like to begin by ensuring in the usual way that the radio equipment is working. Mr. Hadzihasanovic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand? Yes. What about counsel, Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. We can hear and understand interpretation for General Hadzihasanovic. Edina Residovic, lead counsel, Mr. Bourgon, co-counsel, and our court manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Amir Kubura, this is Mr. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic and Mr. Rodney Dixon. And as we've already informed you, our client will not be attending today's Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, for the Prosecution, I am Arthur Buck. With me is co-counsel, Antoinette Issa and our case manager Sebastian Van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I take it those announcements correspond to the appearances. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires that Status Conferences be held for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody at intervals no greater than 120 days. This is the second Status Conference at the appeals stage of this case, and the last Status Conference was held on 1st of September, 2006. This conference, therefore, falls within the 120-day period set by Rule 65 bis. While Mr. Hadzihasanovic is presently in custody at the United Nations Detention Centre, Mr. Kubura was granted early release on 11th April 2006 and was therefore not entitled to a Status Conference under Rule 65 bis. You have already heard counsel saying that Mr. Kubura will not be here today. In the interests of justice, and in order to facilitate the appeals process, Mr. Kubura was, however, invited to be represented at this conference along with Mr. Hadzihasanovic. I'm pleased to see that Mr. Kubura's counsel have joined us for this joint Status Conference. I would like to remind the parties that Status Conferences serve two purposes. First, they allow the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to the appeal and detention conditions. Second, they provide an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. I shall begin with the second of these objectives; namely, an update. This case involves three appeals filed by Mr. Hadzihasanovic, Mr. Kubura, and the Prosecution. On 15 March 2006, Trial Chamber II rendered its judgement in this case. Mr. Kubura filed his notice of appeal from that judgement on 13th April 2006. Mr. Hadzihasanovic filed his notice of appeal on 18th April 2006, and on the same day, the Prosecution filed its notice of appeal. Subsequently, Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura sought extensions of time to file their appeal briefs pending translations of the trial judgement. That judgement had been rendered in French, a language with Mr. Hadzihasanovic and counsel for Mr. Kubura do not speak. So on 27 June 2006, I, as Pre-Appeal Judge granted Mr. Hadzihasanovic's motion seeking an extension of time for submission of his appeal brief until 45 days after the transmission to him of a partial B/C/S translation of the trial judgement with a full translation to be completed subsequently. Mr. Kubura requested the full 75-day period ordinarily allowed under Rule 111 for the appeal brief. He was granted an extension until 60 days after the transmission to his counsel of a certified English translation of the trial judgement. A decision also filed by the Prosecution was entitled to consolidated response brief until 40 days after the second of the two appellant's briefs. Meanwhile, as I have said, the Prosecution filed a notice of appeal on 18th April 2006. It filed an appeal brief on 3 July 2006. Mr. Kubura and Mr. Hadzihasanovic subsequently filed separate motions seeking extensions of time to file the respondents' briefs until 40 days after the transmission of the translations of the trial judgement to Mr. Kubura's counsel and to Mr. Hadzihasanovic respectively. The motions were granted on 26 July and 8 August 2006. Both decisions noted that the Prosecution would be entitled -- be permitted to file a consolidated reply brief within 15 days of the filing of the later of the two response briefs of Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Kubura. This was in keeping with Rule 113 of the Rules and paragraph (C) of the practice direction on the length of briefs and motions. Now, since the last Status Conference in this case, no new motions have been filed in the three appeals. I am pleased to note the translations of the trial judgement in this case are now complete. I have been informed by the court records and support section of the Tribunal that the English translation of the full trial judgement was transmitted to the parties on 23 November 2006 and the B/C/S translation of full judgement was transmitted to the parties on 1 December 2006. Now, unless there has been some misunderstanding about the dates, I will ask Mr. Ibrisimovic and Mr. Dixon, counsel for Mr. Kubura, whether they would confirm receipt of the English translation of the trial judgement on 23 November this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we received the translation of the judgement on the 23rd of November, earlier this year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And I would also ask Mr. Hadzihasanovic whether he would confirm receipt of the B/C/S translation on 1 December this year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Hadzihasanovic himself received the translation of the judgement into B/C/S on the 1st of December, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, then, as the translations have been completed and duly transmitted, the briefing schedule for these appeal proceedings may proceed. I would like to remind counsel for Mr. Hadzihasanovic and counsel for Mr. Kubura that they are required to submit their appeal briefs and respondents' briefs in the Prosecution's appeal in accordance with the time that's set forth in the decisions of 27 June, 26 July, and 8 August 2006. So, do the parties have any remaining concerns in respect of the status of the case? No? Then I take it that the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. On behalf of the accused Hadzihasanovic, we have spoken with the Prosecution this morning and we have compiled those dates in accordance with those decisions that Your Honour has just mentioned, those decisions of 27 June, 26 July, and 8 August. According to this, to those decisions, the -- if I begin with the response which is to be filed by the Defence to the Prosecution brief, our response would be due on the 15th -- sorry, on the 10th of January; that is, for Mr. Hadzihasanovic. As far as our appeals brief, it would have to be filed on the 15th of January. Now, we spoke with the Prosecution this morning, and those dates do not coincide exactly with the dates on which the respondent Kubura has to file his response, nor his appeal, and for the sake of making it easy for all the parties in the courtroom, including Your Honour, and the Appeals Bench we thought that we could harmonise that schedule and get filing dates that would be the same for both respondents in this case and that would make that -- the response brief could be filed by both parties on the 10th of January, whereby Mr. Kubura would be granted a few days additional in order to file his response brief at the same time as the Hadzihasanovic brief. And as far as the appeals brief is concerned, instead of filing on the 15th of January, Mr. Hadzihasanovic would be granted a few additional days and both parties would file on the 22nd of January. This is a submission that we propose, Mr. President, in light of the winter recess coming along and the difficulties in meeting with Mr. Hadzihasanovic over this period, and we discussed this with the Prosecution and it is our understanding that they agree to this proposed schedule. Of course the others can -- we can verify with both the Prosecution and counsel for Mr. Kubura whether this schedule is a joint proposition which I believe it is. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Would counsel for Mr. Kubura say whether he supports this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, we do endorse that proposal. At present, our response to the Prosecution brief is due, in fact, on the 1st of January, and hence the request to harmonise it with that for Mr. Hadzihasanovic to file on the 10th of January, only a few days later. So we would support that proposal fully, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would the Prosecution confirm that it accepts the proposals?

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have accepted these proposals. May I clarify. We talked about the 22nd of January. I think that's actually a Sunday, so the 23rd of January would be more sensible for that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon shakes my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Unless I've my calendar is wrong, I've got the 22nd as being Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: I'm looking at the 2006 calendar, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It's the 2007 calendar, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: My abject apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, then, that is agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: There was one thing I didn't bring one with Defence counsel at the time. During this period, the appeals section of the ICTY will be having a joint appeals advocacy training programme lasting seven days with the appeals sections of ICTR and ICC, and this will fall during the period in which we would file the reply. May we respectfully request an additional five days for the consolidated reply until the 30th of January?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let's see how Mr. Bourgon and counsel for Mr. Kubura react to that. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we fully agree with the proposition by counsel for the Prosecution. If it can help them in filing a joint -- I don't think that this file date delay will cause much of a delay in the hearing of the appeal, and if it can help them, then for sure then we agree to -- for the sake of good cooperation with the Prosecution. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would counsel for Mr. Kubura --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no objection to that proposal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then that is agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BUCK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, conditions of detention. Would Mr. Hadzihasanovic have any concerns about this? THE APPELLANT HADZIHASANOVIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My answer is very brief. Everything is tolerable: The conditions of detention, the food, as well as my health. Everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If there are no other matters, and I see none, I would bring these proceedings to an end and the adjournment at this time. Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
